第 7 章 Career Development for Startup Engineers创业公司工程师的职业发展

Josh Tyler / 乔什·泰勒

— 第 31 页 —

In the early days of a startup, not too many people are concerned with "career development." They're too busy trying to keep the lights on and hit the next milestone, which can have life-or-death consequences for the company.

创业公司早期，没什么人关心「职业发展」。大家都忙着维持公司运转、达成下一个里程碑——这可是生死攸关的事。

But after people have been with the company for a year or two and things have stabilized to the point that they can think more long term about their career, they will. They want to continue growing and are looking for a path. (Side note: hopefully you hired people who want to grow.) If they don't see that path within your team, they will look outside.

但当人们在公司待了一两年、情况稳定到可以开始考虑长期职业发展时，他们就会想了。他们想继续成长，在找一条路径。（顺便说：希望你招的是想成长的人。）如果他们在你的团队里看不到这条路，就会去外面找。

Here are some ways to provide career development:

以下是一些提供职业发展的方式：

  • Share the opportunity to work on larger projects分享参与更大项目的机会
  • Create more specialization创造更多专业方向
  • Hire experienced mentors雇佣有经验的导师
  • Invest in training and classes投资培训和课程

If your company is growing, so are the size and scope of your projects. Share the opportunity to lead these projects, especially with your top performers. You don't need to do it all. In fact, you shouldn't. Is there an upcoming effort to add language support and internationalize the product? Perfect, ask a promising senior engineer if they can lead it. As Laszlo Bock, author of Work Rules! and former senior vice president of people operations at Google says, "You want to give people a little more freedom than you're comfortable with."

如果公司在成长，项目的规模和范围也在变大。把领导这些项目的机会分享出去，尤其是给你的高绩效员工。你不需要什么都自己做。事实上，你不应该什么都自己做。接下来是不是要做多语言支持和产品国际化？太好了，问一个有潜力的高级工程师能不能负责。正如 Google 前人力运营高级副总裁、《Work Rules!》作者 Laszlo Bock 所说：「你要给人们比你觉得舒服的程度再多一点的自由。」

— 第 32 页 —

Early stage startups typically don't require specialization. Rather, they require generalists who can do a bit of everything to solve the most pressing questions each day. If you only have one or two engineers in a web startup, they better know a bit about the backend, the frontend, the database, and server ops.

早期创业公司通常不需要专家。他们需要的是多面手——每天什么都懂一点来解决最紧迫的问题。如果你做 Web 创业公司只有一两个工程师，他们最好后端、前端、数据库、服务器运维都懂一点。

As the team grows, though, more specialization is required. The level of server ops knowledge to handle 1,000 requests per day is very different than the level required for 10,000 requests per second—even with virtualization in Amazon. It's the same for other technical areas. At some point, a generalist isn't enough.

但随着团队扩大，就需要更多专业分工了。每天处理 1000 个请求所需的运维知识水平，和每秒 10000 个请求所需的完全不同——即使有 Amazon 的虚拟化也是如此。其他技术领域也一样。到了某个阶段，多面手就不够用了。

The good news is that most people on your team probably want to be (or already are) an expert in some area. They see specialization as the opportunity to work on the most difficult and most impactful technical problems. (By contrast, a dedicated generalist is probably more motivated by working on the hardest business problems.) Indeed, some people will be able to develop specialized skills out of their own initiative. Some, however, will need help, which is where hiring and training can make a difference.

好消息是，你团队里大多数人可能都想成为（或者已经是）某个领域的专家。他们把专业分工看作是解决最难、最有影响力的技术问题的机会。（相比之下，一个专注的多面手可能更被解决最难的业务问题所驱动。）确实，有些人能主动发展专业技能。但有些人需要帮助——这就是招聘和培训能发挥作用的地方。

One of the biggest hiring shifts you will see with your team is the need to hire into more specialized roles, for the same reasons as I just mentioned. Your projects are becoming more complicated and require more specific expertise. Your search for a "software engineer" turns into "frontend engineer," "backend engineer," "site reliability engineer," "systems engineer," and so on—not to mention all of the different levels of possible experience (such as senior, staff, or principal).

你会看到团队招聘最大的转变之一是需要招更专业的岗位，原因和我刚才说的一样。你的项目越来越复杂，需要更专业的知识。你从招「软件工程师」变成了招「前端工程师」「后端工程师」「站点可靠性工程师」「系统工程师」等等——更不用说不同经验级别了（高级、资深、首席等）。

Creating specialized roles actually makes hiring easier in a couple ways. First, it allows you to post more roles. This might sound simplistic, but circulating more unique job listings will increase the overall number of people you hear from.

设立专业岗位实际上在几个方面让招聘更容易。首先，它让你可以发布更多职位。这听起来可能很简单，但发布更多独特的职位列表会增加你收到的简历总量。

Second, it allows you to more precisely target your recruiting, which makes it easier to source and screen people based on their skills and experience. A search for engineers with at least five years of experience and knowledge of React and TypeScript will turn up fewer results than simply "frontend developer," but the ones you find are more likely to be a match. To borrow terminology from the field of information retrieval, you can improve your precision without much loss in recall.

其次，它让你更精准地定位招聘，更容易根据技能和经验来物色和筛选人。搜索「至少五年经验、懂 React 和 TypeScript 的工程师」比简单搜「前端开发」结果少，但找到的人更可能匹配。借用信息检索领域的术语：你可以在不怎么损失召回率的情况下提升精准率。

Finally, you can promote career development through investment in training programs. Offering an educational assistance program is a great start, but on its own isn't enough. People need to use it. Some people have the drive to find programs on their own, but others need more help and encouragement. Either way, some commitment is required. If you make the courses free for all employees, they'll sign up quickly but rarely complete them. They need to have some kind of vested interest, which could be as simple as getting manager approval, thereby creating an emotional commitment.

最后，你可以通过投资培训项目来促进职业发展。提供教育补贴是个好的开始，但光有这个不够。人们需要真正去用它。有些人有动力自己找课程，但另一些人需要更多帮助和鼓励。不管怎样，都需要某种承诺。如果你给所有员工免费课程，他们会很快报名但很少完成。他们需要某种既得利益——简单如获得经理批准，就能创造一种情感上的承诺。

— 第 33 页 —

It might take a while to see the benefits of learning programs in your team's work, but remember—now you're playing the long game.

要在团队工作中看到学习项目的好处可能需要一段时间，但记住——你现在打的是持久战。
